title: Fats Pichon's band in 1935 and its members
summary: From a 1935 Chicago Defender notice, they go through Pichon's sidemen (Joe Barnes, George Clark, Peabody, Monnier) and whether he was there.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Yeah. I found out in the Chicago Defender, on January the 19th, 1935, they had Fats Pichon's band in Memphis, at the old plantation nightclub. You remember that? Yeah. That joint up there? Yeah. They got Raymond Brown? Yeah. Joe Ball, do you know Joe Ball? Joe Barnes. Oh, Joe Barnes? Yeah.
What did he play?
Trumpet. Robert Carroll? Robert Carroll? Yeah. Robert Carroll?
Yeah.

These might be the same guys that are in the picture, you see. Yeah. And what did Robert Carroll play? I was in the big trouble. Did you know Hayward Walker? We don't know if they were by the names of them.
Yeah. But they had nicknames I guess.
Yeah. And what about Walter Robinson? Did you know him? No, I don't know him.

Luther West? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, second breath. He could do anything with music, man. He died a couple of years ago in New York.
What about George Clark? You know him?
Yeah, he died a couple of months ago.
Really?
He was close with me with George Clark.
Where he's from?
From here.
And who did he play with?
Pichon.
Oh, I see. And he played alto or tenor or baritone or what?
He played tenor.
And Lester Peabody? Huh?
Lester Peabody.
Did you know him? He was supposed to be a saxophone player with Pichon.
Lester Peabody. Yeah. I remember him.
Fred Monner. Fred Monner?
Yeah. That's a guitar player.
Yeah. And Chester's artist?
That's a bass player. And Judge Rowley.
That's a drummer.
Yeah, I see.
Yeah. Well, at least we got that down for one day. Huh? We got that down out of the newspaper. Yeah. From 1935.
Yeah.
You were working with Pichon in 1935?
I believe I was. I don't know.
Yeah. Yeah, well we found it in the newspaper, you see.
Yeah, I believe I was.
